tests.fail_or_repair: Open a user-system docket and downgrade compliance rows to denominator evidence.
tests.label: User, premise, and system identity
tests.question: Does the packet identify household/facility, service address, PWSID or private well/septic edge, premise plumbing, vulnerable users, and responsible owners before accepting a water status?

tests.fail_or_repair: Treat plant/service status as incomplete until operating and sanitation records are joined.
tests.label: Operating state and pressure
tests.question: Can source water, treatment, pressure, storage, distribution, staffing, chemicals, backup power, and wastewater/sewer state be reconstructed for the relevant period?

tests.fail_or_repair: Mark federal/state data as source posture, not tap safety, until current local records are joined.
tests.label: Compliance data boundary
tests.question: Are SDWIS, ECHO, CCR, lab, public-notice, and enforcement rows separated by date, source role, and currentness?

tests.fail_or_repair: Do not treat inventory or rule compliance as lead exposure reduction; open a lead-tap repair file.
tests.label: Lead and premise plumbing
tests.question: Does the packet join lead service line, galvanized/premise plumbing, schools/child care, filters, flushing, replacement, disturbance, and post-work sampling evidence?

tests.fail_or_repair: Do not treat a final/proposed rule or extension as exposure reduction without treatment and interim-water proof.
tests.label: PFAS and chemical risk
tests.question: Are PFAS/chemical test results, treatment, disposal, public notice, vulnerable-population advice, funding, and compliance clocks joined?

tests.fail_or_repair: Treat advisory posting as incomplete until receipt and alternate-water logistics are proven.
tests.label: Advisory reach and alternate water
tests.question: Did boil, do-not-drink, or do-not-use advisories reach affected users in usable formats with bottled water, formula/dialysis/medical, school, shelter, care, and sanitation support?

tests.fail_or_repair: Do not treat drinking-water compliance or NPDES status as sanitation continuity without sewer/septic/stormwater proof.
tests.label: Wastewater, septic, and stormwater
tests.question: Are wastewater treatment, sewer overflow, septic failure, stormwater/flood intrusion, sanitation in congregate settings, and cleanup records joined to public-health risk?

tests.fail_or_repair: Treat certification as a planning signal only; require executable emergency-water proof.
tests.label: Emergency, climate, and AWIA readiness
tests.question: Can AWIA RRA/ERP, mutual aid, alternate source, tankers, backup power, fuel, chemicals, operators, drought/flood/wildfire/heat, and priority users be tested?

tests.fail_or_repair: Do not treat cyber guidance or checklist completion as resilient water without utility-specific controls and recovery proof.
tests.label: Cyber/OT and supplier resilience
tests.question: Are remote access, authentication, OT segmentation, vendor access, manual operation, incident response, and recovery proof joined to water service continuity?

tests.fail_or_repair: Open an affordability/remedy docket before treating service account or assistance page as water access.
tests.label: Affordability, shutoff, remedy, and equity
tests.question: Are rates, arrears, shutoffs, payment plans, low-income/vulnerable protections, bottled-water costs, complaints, reimbursement, repair receipts, and equity denominators joined?

use_rule: Run water/sanitation tests whenever drinking-water system rows, SDWIS/ECHO data, Consumer Confidence Reports, lead service line inventories, PFAS rules, boil/do-not-drink/do-not-use advisories, AWIA risk/resilience plans, wastewater/septic/stormwater records, water shutoffs, affordability burdens, cyber/OT incidents, emergency supply, or critical-facility water dependencies can determine whether people actually have safe water and sanitation. Separate user, premise, source, treatment, contaminant, notice, wastewater, emergency, cyber, affordability, and remedy states before treating a compliance row, report, inventory, permit, or certification as safe water.
